title: Mirror World Escape
covers: how to reflect a point across the x-axis (the y-coordinate changes sign), across the y-axis (the x-coordinate changes sign), and across both axes
cert: reflecting points across the x-axis and the y-axis on the coordinate plane

intro.caption: Lesson 7-9 — reflecting points across the axes. Floor −9 is the Mirror World. Two glass walls cross in the middle of the room. To open the exit, every crystal must be matched with its mirror twin.

balloons.t: The glass walls sit right on the x-axis and the y-axis. Every crystal needs its reflection on the other side.
Mirrors everywhere! Kwame, walk slowly. Kwame? KWAME!
The crystal is at (4, 3). The x-axis is a mirror, so I changed the x: (−4, 3). Ow.
The x-axis goes across. My twin is under it, not beside it. Up and down flips the y!

pages.caption: Across the x-axis, a point flips up or down, so the y changes sign: (x, y) → (x, −y). Across the y-axis, a point flips left or right, so the x changes sign: (x, y) → (−x, y).

balloons.t: Same distance from the mirror, other side. Up 3 becomes down 3!
This one uses the y-axis mirror. It flips left to right.
Left to right. Not into the glass. Got it.
This crystal goes through BOTH mirrors. One flip, then the other.
Two mirrors means two bonks. I'm just going to watch.
Mirror map for sale! It says over the x-axis, change the x. Very shiny. Mostly right.
No thanks. We check our own mirrors.

win.ch: Chapter 4 · Out of the Mirror World

balloons.t: My nose and I are leaving now.
Every crystal found its twin. And Kwame's nose survived!

win.caption: A reflection stays the same distance from the mirror line. Over the x-axis, only y changes sign. Over the y-axis, only x changes sign. Over both, both signs change.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Over the x-Axis
gates.badge: Mirror Reader — Reflect Over the x-Axis
gates.prompt: The first crystal sits at (4, 3). Its twin is its reflection across the x-axis.
hints: Conceptual: the x-axis is the line going across. A flip over it sends a point straight up or down, so it stays at the same x.
Procedural: keep x the same. Change the sign of y.

steps: Practice crystal: (1, 6). The mirror is the x-axis.
The point flips straight down, so x stays 1.
y changes sign: 6 becomes −6. The twin is (1, −6).

items.q: Tap the twin of (4, 3) across the x-axis.

fb.msg: That's Kwame's twin, (−4, 3). You changed x, which is a flip over the y-axis. Over the x-axis, only y changes.
You changed both signs. That flips over both axes. Over the x-axis, x stays 4.
That's (3, 4): x and y swapped. A reflection never swaps them. Keep x = 4 and change the sign of y.
That's the crystal itself. Its twin is on the other side of the x-axis.

items.fbDefault: Keep x = 4. The twin is 3 units BELOW the x-axis.

options.fb: Changing x flips the point left to right, across the y-axis. The x-axis flips up and down.
Both signs change only when you reflect across both axes. One mirror, one sign.
That's the same point. A reflection moves it to the other side of the mirror.

gates.pass: The crystal at (4, −3) lights up under the glass. Kwame holds an ice pack to his nose.

gates.title: Gate 2 · Over the y-Axis
gates.badge: Side Flipper — Reflect Over the y-Axis
gates.prompt: The next crystal is at (−5, −1). Its twin is across the y-axis.
hints: Conceptual: the y-axis is the line going up and down. A flip over it sends a point straight left or right, so it stays at the same y.
Procedural: keep y the same. Change the sign of x.

steps: Practice crystal: (2, 4). The mirror is the y-axis.
The point flips straight left, so y stays 4.
x changes sign: 2 becomes −2. The twin is (−2, 4).

items.q: Tap the twin of (−5, −1) across the y-axis.

fb.msg: That's (−5, 1). You changed y, which is a flip over the x-axis. Over the y-axis, only x changes.
You changed both signs. That flips over both axes. Over the y-axis, y stays −1.
That's (−1, −5): x and y swapped. Keep y = −1 and change the sign of x.

items.fbDefault: Keep y = −1. The twin is 5 units to the RIGHT of the y-axis.

items.label: How many units apart are (−5, −1) and its twin?
items.aria: distance between the crystal and its reflection

fb.msg: 5 is the distance from the crystal to the mirror. The twin is 5 more on the other side.
The twin is on the other side of the y-axis, not in the same spot. From x = −5 to x = 5 is how far?
Right size, wrong sign. Distance is never negative.

items.fbDefault: The crystal is 5 units left of the mirror and the twin is 5 units right of it.

gates.pass: The twin at (5, −1) glows, 10 units away: 5 to the mirror and 5 more. The mirror sits exactly halfway.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Both Mirrors
gates.badge: Double Flipper — Reflect Over Both Axes
gates.prompt: Bao's crystal at (2, 5) flips across the x-axis, then across the y-axis.
hints: Conceptual: each mirror changes one sign. Two mirrors change both signs.
Procedural: first flip: change the sign of y. Second flip: change the sign of x. Write the point after each flip.

steps: Across the x-axis: (−1, −3). Then across the y-axis: (1, −3).
Both signs changed, so (−1, 3) lands at (1, −3).

items.q: Tap where Bao's crystal at (2, 5) lands after both flips.

fb.msg: That's after the x-axis flip only. Now flip across the y-axis too: change the sign of x.
That's after the y-axis flip only. Now flip across the x-axis too: change the sign of y.
That's (−5, −2): x and y swapped. Change both signs but keep the order: (−2, −5).
That's (5, 2): x and y swapped, and no flip at all. Change the signs, not the order.

items.fbDefault: Change the sign of y, then the sign of x.

items.q: Two crystals are at (−4, 1) and (−4, −1). Which mirror makes them twins?

options.fb: x stayed −4 and y changed sign. That is an up-and-down flip, across the x-axis.
Both axes would change both signs. Only y changed here.
They are the same distance, 1 unit, from the x-axis on opposite sides. That is a reflection.

gates.pass: (2, 5) lands at (−2, −5) after two flips, and Bao spots the x-axis twins. Kwame watches from a safe distance.

gates.title: Boss Gate · The Mirror Gate
gates.prompt: The gate shows a triangle of crystals: A (1, 2), B (5, 2) and C (1, 6). Reflect the whole triangle across the x-axis to fill the three sockets.
hints: Conceptual: to reflect a shape, reflect each vertex. Across the x-axis, every vertex keeps its x.
Procedural: for each point, keep x and change the sign of y. Grimble's map changes x, so don't trust it.

steps: Practice triangle: (−2, 1), (−5, 1), (−2, 4). Reflect it across the y-axis.
Keep each y and change the sign of each x.

items.q: Tap all three reflected vertices: the twins of A (1, 2), B (5, 2) and C (1, 6) across the x-axis.

fb.msg: That's (−1, 2), Grimble's trap. Changing x reflects across the y-axis. Across the x-axis, keep x and change y.
That's (−5, 2). You changed x. Across the x-axis, B keeps x = 5 and y becomes −2.
That's (−1, 6). You changed x. Across the x-axis, C keeps x = 1 and y becomes −6.
That's (−1, −2). You changed both signs. Across the x-axis, only y changes.
That's (2, −1): you swapped A's numbers to (2, 1) and then reflected. Keep x = 1: A's twin is (1, −2).

items.fbDefault: You need three points. Keep each x and change the sign of each y.

items.q: Grimble's map says (−3, 4) across the x-axis is (3, 4). Who is right?

options.t: Grimble. Across the x-axis, x changes sign.
options.fb: That's Grimble's mistake. (3, 4) is the reflection across the y-axis.
(3, −4) changes both signs. That reflects across both axes.
That swaps x and y. A reflection never swaps the coordinates.

options.t: Grimble is wrong. It should be (−3, −4).

items.q: Last lock: which pair are reflections across the y-axis?

options.fb: Here y changed sign and x stayed the same. That's a reflection across the x-axis.
Those just swap x and y. That's not a reflection across an axis.
Both signs changed. That's a reflection across both axes.

gates.pass: KRRRNK. Three crystals click into (1, −2), (5, −2) and (1, −6). Grimble's mirror map cracks right down the middle.

journal.heading: Lesson 7-9 — what the Mirror World taught us
rows: The point flips up or down. x stays, y changes sign: (4, 3) → (4, −3).
The point flips left or right. y stays, x changes sign: (−5, −1) → (5, −1).
A twin is as far from the mirror as the point is. (−5, −1) and (5, −1) are each 5 units from the y-axis, 10 units apart.
He changed x to reflect across the x-axis and got (−4, 3). Across the x-axis, the y changes.
journal.quote: "The mirror on the x-axis flips the y. Weird, but true. Trust me, I glow." — Pip

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 7-9 (Reflect Points Across Axes) as one focused read. Whole-class on a projector, pairs on devices, or independent practice. It covers only this lesson: reflecting points across the x-axis (y changes sign), across the y-axis (x changes sign), across both axes, and reflecting the vertices of a shape.
standards: Recognize that ordered pairs differing only by signs are reflections across one or both axes
